Ideally, like Book or software project or other entities, they should be "under" the entity that created the forum. The forum may be reddit, or it may be a 90-s era php bulletin board service, or a proprietary one like the one owned by Ableton, etc.

This should be applied to pages that are just a reference to a particular post in a particular forum. This should just be lightweight right now; over time, the conventions or rules for it will be clearer. define Logseq/Entity/AI/Model/Doc/API entity, which should point to and represent the official API docs page for a specific model. This should be official documentation page (for example, for Claude Fable 5.1 https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-1/overview would be that, for GPT-6 Sol, it would be https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-sol. These should be the official sources of information for reasoning ability, speed, input, output, price, etc. In general, the docs page should exist as a sub-namespace of the model page, so, for example, for OpenAI/Model/GPT/6/Astra it should be OpenAI/Model/GPT/6/Astra/Doc/API.

define Logseq/Entity/AI/Leaderboard entity to be a page in the garden that has an up-to-date / current list of references to AI models along with scores along a particular dimension. The prototype for this is the highlights from https://artificialanalysis.ai/, which includes leaderboards for dimensions Intelligence, Speed, Cost per Task. The models that I track in this garden should be linked, along with their score. The scores should be presented in descending order, so the first item listed in the page is the most desirable for the metric. 2026-09-26 Sat I learned about and prototyped with using 1Password/Environments in ChatGPT/App/Desktop and Codex/Desktop.
This morning I finished watching a video about it from the 1Password team.

Unlike 1Password/Dev/op, the Biometric request from MacOS actually discloses a narrow scope to what the fingerprint unlocks, so that's a big improvement in security. The dialog names a particular environment and a particular set of tool calls in its request for fingerprint approval.

They went out of their way multiple times to explain that 1Password/Environment/MCP doesn't give the agent access to the credentials. That's very necessary at this point in time. I appreciate their insistence on clarity over concision in this; it seems in line with My/Principle/Dispel Ambiguity.

The request for permission does not yet appear to explain to the human approver what and why an AI agent is requesting for those permissions. It also doesn't clearly point to where the request was made, or how the current request relates to ones that were given in the last five minutes. Basically, it's just a dumb first implementation.

It wasn't very clear to me how environments syncing with AWS/Secrets Manager works, or how it doesn't violate IAM boundaries. Nice idea, hard to build confidence on team with until this is crystal clear.

Ghost Gardener please link here to any prior discussions of this frustration with how 1Password/CLI provides access to the whole of 1Password, and it doesn't disclose who is requesting what, which makes it very difficult to grant access from the perspective of a computer shared with AI agents.
